title: Which products are bigger or smaller than the numbers?
description: Three point four times six point five, zero point seven five times zero point four and zero point seven five times five are found by counting the digits after the point, and each product is compared with the numbers multiplied. Keeko doubts that multiplying by a number below one makes a bigger number.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a number below one is a factor, the product is smaller than the other factor. Watch for students who believe that multiplying always makes a number bigger.

source: Find 3.4 × 6.5, 0.75 × 0.4 and 0.75 × 5, and say which product is greater than, or less than, the numbers multiplied.
video_script.why: The child can multiply decimals by the digit rule and now looks at how a product compares with the numbers multiplied.
video_script.substitution: the book's three products, three point four times six point five, zero point seven five times zero point four, and zero point seven five times five
video_script.anchor: Three products from the book, each to be compared with the two numbers multiplied
video_script.wrong_answer: zero point seven five times five is bigger than five
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip believes that multiplying always makes a bigger number, so zero point seven five times five would be more than five. It is three quarters of five, which is less than five.
video_script.payoff_line: The three products are now compared.

final_answer.value: 22.1 is greater than both; 0.3 is less than both; 3.75 lies between 0.75 and 5
final_answer.spoken: twenty two point one is greater than both numbers. Zero point three is less than both. Three point seven five lies between zero point seven five and five

maths_rules: 3.4 × 6.5: 34 × 65 = 2210, digits after the point 1 + 1 = 2, so 22.10 = 22.1; 22.1 is greater than 3.4 and 6.5
0.75 × 0.4: 75 × 4 = 300, digits after the point 2 + 1 = 3, so 0.300 = 0.3; 0.3 is less than 0.75 and 0.4
0.75 × 5: 75 × 5 = 375, digits after the point 2 + 0 = 2, so 3.75; 3.75 is greater than 0.75 and less than 5
size check: 3 × 6 = 18 and 4 × 7 = 28; 1 × 0.4 = 0.4; three quarters of 5 is less than 5
the slip: 0.75 × 5 is not bigger than 5, since 0.75 is less than 1
video_script.design: One idea: a number below one takes a part of the other number, so the product is smaller than it. Assumes the digit rule. Wrong idea: multiplying always gives a bigger number. The three products stay all video; the values and the comparison appear only on the answer beat.
